title: In Jharkhand’s SIR, Everyone Who Gets a Notice Pays For it
shows: A research intern with Jean Dreze reports from the hearings at the Ranchi collectorate on 2 September, from two booth level officers, one at a booth in urban Ranchi and one at a rural booth in Bagodar, and from the published lists of unmapped electors for two booths in Hatia. He reports that people who came with only a voter ID card and Aadhaar were asked for a caste or residence certificate, and that stalls outside drew up affidavits for Rs 300 to Rs 500 each, most of a day's minimum wage for unskilled work in Jharkhand's larger cities, though as far as he could tell most were not needed. He reports that about two in five of the 172 unmapped electors on the two Hatia lists are women recorded only through a husband's name, and that over half of them are 41 or older. The booth level officers name migrant workers, women who cannot produce a parent's entry, the elderly and tenants as the electors most easily lost, and describe an Election Commission portal that often goes down. He cites the Chief Electoral Officer's office for 63,24,116 electors on the draft roll to be served notices, and for Hatia as the constituency with the most notices, 1,52,362. He says the account rests on two booths, two booth level officers and one visit, and makes no claim beyond them.
quote: The Chief Electoral Officer’s office said 63,24,116 voters on it would be served notices, close to three in ten of the names on the draft roll.
Sixty-three lakh voters have been told to prove their electoral status, and proving it costs time and money.

title: Bengal faces fresh electoral roll revision amid 21 lakh pending SIR deletion appeals
shows: The Federal reports that West Bengal's summary revision, with its draft due on 23 November and its final roll on 16 January 2027, begins while appeals against deletions after the adjudication of logical discrepancies are still pending before the appellate tribunals, more than 21.7 lakh of them by its count. It cites the Civic Research Group's analysis of the Commission's data and tribunal records for more than 27 lakh electors deleted after adjudication, with nearly 21 lakh of those who appealed still awaiting a decision. It reports that estimates from different sets of records put the electors still marked under adjudication, with no final order they could appeal, at around 30,000, and sets that against the Chief Electoral Officer's office's count of 815 undecided cases and 5,004 decisions awaiting e-signatures. It reports that booth level officers have been asked to visit electors who were on the rolls before the revision and are missing now, and to help those eligible apply on Form 6. The general secretary of an association of booth level officers said they had not been told to use a new facility in the BLO app for uploading documents in tribunal cases. The paper reports from party sources that a BJP team of about 200 leaders will visit all 294 Assembly constituencies from 26 November to record views on the revision.
quote: But the new exercise has been initiated even as more than 21.7 lakh appeals against deletions on grounds of logical discrepancies are still pending before appellate tribunals.
The West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer’s office, however, put the number of undecided cases at just 815 across the state, while another 5,004 decisions were awaiting electronic signatures.
